subject: Re: Night-shift escalation & temporary P2 carveout request
messages:
From: Alex Wu <alex.wu@fastcommerce.com>
To: tessa_morgan@redwood.com
Cc: support@fastcommerce.com
Date: Tue, 16 Jan 2029 19:04:00 -0800
Subject: Night shift coverage & escalation path — temporary exception request

Hi Tessa,

We have a migration window coming up (internal note: Dec 28 — Jan 20) where our infra team will be running cross-region data moves. The migration pushes a lot of our maintenance into the 00:00–06:00 PST window.

Our ask: can Redwood approve a temporary exception to the P2 overnight response SLA for the migration period? We’d like to extend P2 response to 8 hours during nights (00:00–06:00) for three weeks. P1 responses remain unchanged.

Attached is a proposed on-call rotation from our side and a draft of the changes we’d sign. We also need clarity on the escalation ladder — who at Redwood will be the bridging contact overnight if our oncall needs escalation?

Thanks,
Alex Wu
Platform Ops, FastCommerce
attachments: proposed_oncall_rotation.xlsx, SLA_amendment_draft.docx
From: tessa_morgan@redwood.com <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
To: Alex Wu <alex.wu@fastcommerce.com>
Cc: sean_gallagher@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 16 Jan 2029 20:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Night shift coverage & escalation path — temporary exception request

Hi Alex — thanks for the clear ask and the attachments. Tagging Sean and Marissa so we can scope operational and contract approvals.

Quick next steps from our side:
- Sean: can you confirm the overnight bridging contact and the oncall escalation play?
- Marissa: can you confirm whether a 3-week P2 extension is approvable on a provisional basis and what guardrails we need in the SLA amendment?

Alex, a few clarifying Qs for you:
- Will FastCommerce maintain an on-call PDT person to triage before escalation?
- Who will be the single point of contact for DocuSign?

If we agree to a provisional carveout we’ll require: retention of full request traces/telemetry for the period, a rollback trigger (error > X%), and a named Redwood bridging contact.

Thanks — I’ll aim to get an internal decision by end of day tomorrow.

—Tessa Morgan
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
From: Alex Wu <alex.wu@fastcommerce.com>

Tessa, Sean, Marissa —

Thanks for the quick reply. Answers below:
- Yes, FastCommerce will have a named PDT on-call (I will be the daytime coordinator; nights will be handled by Priya S. — priya.s@fastcommerce.com).
- DocuSign contact: me (alex.wu@fastcommerce.com).

I uploaded the proposed rotation spreadsheet to the Drive link and attached the same file. We propose the following guardrails:
- Carveout duration: 21 days starting 2029-01-28
- P2 night window: 00:00–06:00 PST, response extended to 8 hours; P1 unchanged
- Rollback trigger: any night where P1 still experiences >3 incidents or where latency regressions exceed 20% relative to baseline for two consecutive nights

We’d like Redwood’s overnight bridging contact to be an escalation alias (e.g., oncall@redwood.com) plus a named SRE lead for priority escalations.

Attachments: proposed_oncall_rotation.xlsx

Best,
Alex
From: marissa_cole@redwood.com <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Wu <alex.wu@fastcommerce.com>, tessa_morgan@redwood.com
Cc: sean_gallagher@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 17 Jan 2029 11:37:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Night shift coverage & escalation path — temporary exception request

Alex — thanks for the specifics. We can provisionally approve a time-limited P2 response extension under the following conditions (please confirm in writing so we can generate the DocuSign amendment):

1) Observable guardrails must be in place and accessible to both teams:
   - Full request/telemetry retention for the carveout window
   - Nightly automated health summary delivered to both teams by 08:00 PST
2) Rollback conditions (as you proposed) must be automated and enforced (errors and latency thresholds)
3) Redwood will require a signed amendment to your contract covering the 21-day carveout and the rollback policy
4) If any P1 impact occurs more than twice in the 21-day window, Redwood reserves the right to terminate the carveout immediately

When we have Alex’s written acceptance and the Drive folder with the rotation + runbook, I’ll put the amendment into DocuSign and copy legal for a quick review.

Regards,
Marissa Cole
Head of Customer Success Operations
Redwood Inference
attachments: runbook_excerpt.txt
From: sean_gallagher@redwood.com <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>

Date: Thu, 18 Jan 2029 09:54:00 -0800

Alex — quick operational note.

Redwood bridging contact for nights: oncall@redwood.com (alias routed to the overnight SRE rotation). For highest-severity escalation (P1-level escalation during the carveout) the ladder is:

- Step 1: FastCommerce night triage (Priya S.) tries to remediate within 30 minutes
- Step 2: FastCommerce escalates to oncall@redwood.com with link to the incident trace
- Step 3: Redwood overnight SRE takes initial action; if not resolved in 1 hour, escalation to Redwood SRE lead (sean_gallagher@redwood.com) and paging to the Day Ops lead

I’ve attached a short excerpt from our runbook that shows the expected format for the incident trace link and required fields (timestamp, request id, top-level error class). Please ensure the traces are included in your nightly health summary.

—Sean
